html:
The map's label, in 1880 and 1900, for the states of the Nyamwezi and Kimbu peoples of west central Tanzania, on the main caravan route from the coast to Lake Tanganyika. Three powers stood out.

  • Unyanyembe, a Nyamwezi chiefdom, held Tabora, the inland base of the Arab and Swahili traders from Zanzibar.
  • Urambo, built by Mirambo, a Nyamwezi chief who used gangs of gun-carrying fighters, called ruga-ruga, to forge a large state. He fought the Tabora traders from 1871 and for years could close the route. Henry Morton Stanley met him and called him a Napoleon of Africa.
  • Ukimbu, where Nyungu ya Mawe built a similar warrior state among the Kimbu.

Both Mirambo and Nyungu died in 1884. In the 1890s the Germans conquered the region for German East Africa; the chief of Unyanyembe, Isike, died defending his fort in 1893.
